steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on efficient multiuser detection for massive machine-type communication (mMTC) using AMP. Set up the short-packet G-MAC setting, point out the gap in low-complexity MUD, describe our two AMP-based algorithms, list the contributions, and add a short notation paragraph.

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. mMTC
- many IoT applications need mMTC: many devices send very short packets to a BS
- packets sent when a measured value changes -> sporadic traffic
- sparse signal processing for massive connectivity (data + activity detection) already studied

2. G-MAC
- bounds on exact block error probability of Gaussian random codes in AWGN, massive uplink multiple access (MA), finite message length
- same work: G-MAC (Gaussian multiple access channel) promising for massive uplink short packets
- challenge: efficient, low-complexity multiuser detection (MUD) at the BS
- iterative soft interference cancellation (SIC) decoding used for G-MAC short packets, but error propagation

3. Our approach
- two efficient low-complexity MUD algorithms for G-MAC, short-packet mMTC
- MUD as under-determined sparse signal recovery
- approximate message passing (AMP) for soft decoding of packets from IoT devices
- usual: joint prior unknown -> no optimal MMSE denoiser; minimax design for worst-case / least-favorable distribution -> soft-thresholding denoiser
- here: exact and approximate prior joint distribution obtainable
- -> optimal separable and non-separable MMSE denoisers for Bayesian AMP
- decoupling effect -> low-complexity MMSE denoising per AMP iteration

4. Contributions
- G-MAC MUD as sparse recovery; exact + approximate prior; approximate via minimizing Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD)
- two algorithms: relaxed block sparsity AMP (RBS-AMP), block sparsity AMP (BS-AMP)
- multiuser efficiency (MUE) derived, close to one
- BS-AMP: new achievability bound closer to known upper bound than RBS-AMP, state of the art AMP soft decoding, SIC decoding

5. Notation
- (\cdot)^{\rm T}, {\rm Tr}(\cdot), \|\cdot\|_{0}, \|\cdot\|: transpose, trace, 0 -norm, Euclidean norm
- \hat{\bf{x}} estimate of \bf x; \delta(\cdot) Dirac delta

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Many IoT applications need massive machine-type communications (mMTC) services, where a large number of devices send very short packets to a BS. Usually these short packets are sent whenever a measured value changes, so a sporadic traffic pattern is common in mMTC. Sparse signal processing for massive connectivity, including data and activity detection, has been studied in several works.

Recently bounds on the exact block error probability of Gaussian random codes in AWGN for massive uplink multiple access (MA) at finite message length have been derived. That work has also shown that the Gaussian multiple access channel (G-MAC) is a promising solution for supporting massive uplink connectivity for short packet transmission. The hard part in realizing G-MAC is designing efficient and low-complexity multiuser detection (MUD) algorithms at the BS. Iterative soft interference cancellation (SIC) decoding has been used in another work for the G-MAC with short packet transmission, but it suffers from error propagation.

In this paper we propose two efficient and low-complexity MUD algorithms for the G-MAC for short-packet mMTC. First we formulate the MUD problem as an under-determined sparse signal recovery problem. Then we propose to use approximate message passing (AMP) for soft decoding of the short packets sent by the IoT devices in the network. In most MUD problems that use AMP for soft decoding, the joint prior distribution of the vector to be recovered is assumed to be unknown. Then the optimal MMSE denoiser cannot be used, and so the denoiser is designed under the minimax framework to optimize the AMP algorithm performance for the worst-case or least-favorable distribution, which gives a soft-thresholding denoiser. But in our problem the key idea is that we can get the exact and approximate prior joint distribution of the sparse vector to be recovered. So the optimal separable and non-separable MMSE denoisers can be used for Bayesian AMP soft decoding. Because of the decoupling effect the MMSE denoising in each AMP iteration has low complexity. The contributions of the paper are:

- We formulate G-MAC MUD as a sparse signal recovery problem and get the exact and approximate prior joint distribution of the sparse vector to be recovered. We get the approximate prior distribution by minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD), which measures the difference between probability densities.

- Using the exact and the KLD-based approximate prior distribution of the sparse vector, we introduce two MUD algorithms, (i) the relaxed block sparsity AMP (RBS-AMP) and (ii) the block sparsity AMP (BS-AMP) MUD algorithms, for G-MAC, which are suitable for short packet transmission in mMTC.

- We derive the multiuser efficiency (MUE) of the proposed MUD algorithms and show that it is close to one.

- We show that our BS-AMP MUD algorithm gives a new achievability bound that is closer to the upper bound mentioned above than the achievability bound of the RBS-AMP, the state of the art AMP soft decoding from the literature, and the SIC decoding mentioned above.

Notation: The symbols (\cdot)^{\rm T}, {\rm Tr}(\cdot), \|\cdot\|_{0}, and \|\cdot\| are the transpose operator, the trace of a matrix, the 0 -norm, and the Euclidean norm of a vector. \hat{\bf{x}} is an estimate of the vector \bf x, and \delta(\cdot) is the Dirac delta function.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
In many IoT applications, massive machine-type communications (mMTC) services are required, where a large number of devices transmit very short packets to a BS. Typically, these short packets are transmitted whenever a measured value changes; thus, a sporadic traffic pattern is common in mMTC [1,2,3]. Sparse signal processing for massive connectivity, including data and activity detection, has been studied in [3,4,5].

Recently, bounds on the exact block error probability of Gaussian random codes in AWGN for massive uplink multiple access (MA) at finite message length have been derived [6]. The author in [6] has shown that the Gaussian multiple access channel (G-MAC) is a promising solution to support massive uplink connectivity for short packet transmission. The challenging task in the realization of G-MAC is the design of efficient and low-complexity multiuser detection (MUD) algorithms at the BS [7]. In [8], iterative soft interference cancellation (SIC) decoding has been employed for the G-MAC with short packet transmission, but it suffers from error propagation.

In this paper, we propose two efficient and low-complexity MUD algorithms for the G-MAC for short-packet mMTC. We first formulate the MUD problem as an under-determined sparse signal recovery problem. Then, we propose to employ approximate message passing (AMP) for soft decoding of the short packets transmitted by the IoT devices in the network. In most MUD problems using AMP for soft decoding, the joint prior distribution of the vector to be recovered is generally assumed to be unknown. In such cases, the optimal MMSE denoiser cannot be employed, and thus the denoiser is designed under the minimax framework to optimize the AMP algorithm performance for the worst-case or least-favorable distribution, which leads to a soft-thresholding denoiser. However, in the problem at hand, the key idea is that we can obtain the exact and approximate prior joint distribution of the sparse vector to be recovered. Thus, the optimal separable and non-separable MMSE denoisers can be employed for Bayesian AMP soft decoding. The decoupling effect results in low-complexity MMSE denoising in each AMP iteration [9,10,11]. The contributions of the paper are:

- We formulate the problem of G-MAC MUD as a sparse signal recovery problem and obtain the exact and approximate prior joint distribution of the sparse vector to be recovered. The approximate prior distribution is obtained by minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD) as a measure of the difference between probability densities.

- Taking into account the exact and the KLD-based approximate prior distribution of the sparse vector, we introduce two MUD algorithms, called (i) the relaxed block sparsity AMP (RBS-AMP) and (ii) the block sparsity AMP (BS-AMP) MUD algorithms, for G-MAC suitable for short packet transmission in mMTC.

- The multiuser efficiency (MUE) of the proposed MUD algorithms is derived and shown to be close to one.

- We show that our BS-AMP MUD algorithm results in a new achievability bound that is closer to the upper bound in [6] than the achievability bound of the RBS-AMP, the state of the art AMP soft decoding in [12], and the SIC decoding in [8].

Notation: The symbols (\cdot)^{\rm T}, {\rm Tr}(\cdot), \|\cdot\|_{0}, and \|\cdot\| denote the transpose operator, the trace of a matrix, the 0 -norm, and the Euclidean norm of a vector, respectively. The symbol \hat{\bf{x}} is an estimate of the vector \bf x, and \delta(\cdot) is the Dirac delta function.

References:
[1] M. Mohammadkarimi, M. A. Raza, and O. A. Dobre, “Signature-based nonorthogonal massive multiple access for future wireless networks: Uplink massive connectivity for machine-type communications,” IEEE Veh. Technol. Mag. , vol. 13, no. 4, pp. 40–50, Oct. 2018.
